learningObjectives: Use for, while, and do-while loops for repeated operations.
Control loop execution with break and continue.
Choose an appropriate loop structure for a given problem.

activities.title: Loop Execution Flow
activities.instruction: Arrange the stages of a for-loop iteration.

content.concept: A loop evaluates its controlling condition before or after an iteration depending on the loop type. A for loop performs initialization, checks the condition, executes the body, updates the loop variable, and repeats while the condition remains true.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: For Loop Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the components of a Java for loop.

content.concept: A for loop commonly contains initialization, a boolean condition, an update expression, and a body that executes for each iteration.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Initializes the loop variable before the first iteration.
Determines whether another iteration should execute.
Updates the loop variable after each iteration.
The loop body executed during each iteration.

activities.title: Choose the Loop
activities.instruction: Choose the loop structure that best fits each scenario.

content.concept: Use for when iteration is naturally controlled by a counter or known range, while when repetition depends on a condition, and do-while when the body must execute at least once.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Iteration Controller
activities.instruction: Change the loop limit and observe how the number of iterations changes.

content.concept: Changing the loop condition or update expression changes the number of iterations. A loop such as for (int i = 1; i <= n; i++) executes n times when n is positive.
